dependency_policies: Tracing is optional and model-owned. Both model constructors start without a trace; enabled evaluation tracks scalar reads, reference/range results, dynamic/named/structured references and spill edges. Conditional formatting is excluded and spill restarts reset trace state.

Trace rectangles retain empty cells; contained point reads compact into a covering rectangle. Incomplete traces are explicitly refused. Normal calculation uses the same evaluation/cache/spill/chart path without a trace allocation.

Source rectangles use the exact writer resolver. Sparse transitive formula reads intersect current report footprints, producing cache predecessor sets. Cycles are refused before choosing a ready cache; saved order breaks ties.

Each staged refresh triggers a fresh observed graph. Completion timestamps invalidate consumers whose predecessors changed later or became pending, including growth into previously empty dependency cells. Targets deduplicate shared caches; invalidation may require refreshing an affected cache again.

A final traced calculation supplies the exact committed formula caches without another volatile pass after validation. There is no numeric value-convergence loop. Later ordinary calculation may generate a new volatile source sample.

Reference-only operands conservatively overapproximate value dependencies; activated branches are rechecked. This is not a static all-branches or Excel calculation-chain oracle. Resource/retry exhaustion refuses the entire atomic batch.

pivot_authoring_policies: Patch only changed settings; preserve unrelated root/container/entry XML metadata and namespace aliases. Empty optional min-one containers are omitted; unknown wrapper metadata blocks destructive removal.
Source ranges, declared names and tables currently keep the same headers, field count and order. All cache-sharing reports are rebuilt and collision/protection checked before mutation.

One to4096 measures use eleven supported aggregation names. An original measure may occur once; inserted measures receive new identities. Retained chart IDs, styles and plot roles use these identities rather than a changed array position.

Row/column/page placement is unique, Values occurs on one axis, and actual filter labels/values/page geometry participate in report ownership and occupied-cell checks. Old owned body/filter cells alone are cleared during movement.

Member selections use actual stable cache indices. Explicit item refresh populates choices from the current source as its own history step while preserving pending edits; a changed pending source must be applied first. No synthetic member IDs are inferred from raw records.

The common editor refuses stale configuration, changed shared-report count, changed field names or reused/truncated cache-member prefixes. New appended members remain safe. Apply is one staged history edit; no-op Apply does not add history.

Required internal table-to-cache links are preserved or added for unambiguous legacy catalogs. Explicit contradictory, external or ambiguous links are diagnostics and block editing. Foreign namespace lookalikes cannot override ownership.
Known custom/84 preset style names are selectable; style removal retains manually applied cell formats. General page/group/style producer equivalence remains open.
Valid Strict percent gap/overlap values are read numerically. This does not establish full Strict chart authoring or general chart namespace/MCE/schema compatibility.
